storm.summary_layperson: No storm risk expected this evening — skies are quiet, radar is clear, and there's nothing brewing to threaten the cove through 10 PM.
storm.local_effect_blurb: Water is running about 4°F warmer than the air right now, so there's no marine-layer buffer tonight — moot anyway, since no storms are anywhere near the cove.
storm.detail_html:
Radar (KOKX) shows no storm cells within range of the cove this afternoon, and HRRR model CAPE sits at 0 J/kg through the entire forecast window — there is no instability in the atmosphere for storms to build on.

The region's only active weather headline is a Wind Advisory issued by NWS Upton for the wider area, but its onset is tomorrow, September 25 at 2:00 PM — well outside tonight's 5–10 PM window, so it doesn't factor into this evening's risk.

The Sound's usual protective marine layer isn't in play tonight: water (68°F) is actually warmer than the air (64°F and falling), an air–water gap of about -4°F. That's the opposite of the setup needed to stabilize the boundary layer and choke incoming storms — but with nothing on radar and zero CAPE, the point is moot for this window.

Bottom line for the cove: a quiet, storm-free evening. Skies partly sunny, clearing overnight, with no thunderstorm risk expected through 10 PM.

What would change the call: any new convective initiation showing up on radar inbound from the west, or CAPE building above the 1500 J/kg threshold in a later HRRR cycle. Neither is indicated tonight.

wind.regime_label: Moderate gradient wind — no sea breeze in play
wind.tactics_blurb: Moderate NNE gradient wind, no sea breeze in play tonight — wind stays fairly uniform across the course but trends light by the second half of the window, fading from about 10 kt at 5 PM to around 5 kt by 10 PM. Stay center, no strong shift bias expected.
wind.tactics_detail_html:
Today is a gradient-only day — the two-ingredient sea-breeze test fails outright: the inland air is actually about 4°F cooler than the Sound (delta T of -4°F, versus the +5°F needed to build a thermal), and the coastal station ensemble shows 0% southerly flow. There's no thermal component tonight; wind direction and magnitude both track the synoptic gradient (internally, B-moderate).

RYC reads NNE at 6.2 kt instantaneous / 9.5 kt 10-min average, gusting to 16.3, which lines up with the regional gradient wind reported at KBDR (NE, 12 kt) and KHPN (N, 11 kt gusting 17). The authoritative station mean is 11.7 kt, comfortably in the 8–15 kt B-moderate band.

Direction agreement across the full station ensemble is low (0.55), but that's driven by scattered near-calm APRS stations reporting noisy, low-confidence directions, not a genuine split in the wind field — RYC and the HRRR forecast direction stay within about 15° of each other (NNE, 15–24°) all evening.

Per gradient rules, this holds through sunset (6:47 PM) and beyond since it isn't solar-driven, but HRRR's usable forecast only extends to 7:00 PM; the 8–10 PM hours in the table are extrapolated from the softening trend already visible in the model (10 kt at 5 PM down to under 7 kt by 7 PM), consistent with the typical 1–2 kt nocturnal boundary-layer softening expected on a B-moderate evening.

At NNE, the cove sees close to the cleanest offshore-adjacent flow in the geography table — fairly uniform pressure across the course, trending toward light-air conditions (around 5 kt) by the second half of the window. Shift character should stay steady with normal gust/lull cycling rather than any persistent rotation; no frontal signal in the pressure trend or forecast text.

data_caveats: HRRR forecast only extends through 7:00 PM (f01–f04); f05–f12 fetch/parse failed, so the 8–10 PM wind values are extrapolated from the established softening trend, not directly modeled.
